answer.explanation: Identity mapping shows session-red maps to A and session-blue maps to B (obs-1). Policy context is unavailable (obs-2), so the access-control policy prerequisite required to determine authorized vs unauthorized object access cannot be established. Endpoint responses for all principal/selector combinations return status 200 with body error "not authorized" and an object whose owner matches the selector value: session-red with selector A returns owner A record-A (obs-3); session-red with selector B returns owner B record-B (obs-4); session-blue with selector A returns owner A record-A (obs-5); session-blue with selector B returns owner B record-B (obs-6). The header selector is processed, changing the returned object, but no request yields a legitimate authorized baseline and the policy mapping needed to confirm principal A is not authorized for object B is missing. Without a documented policy and a legitimate baseline, an authorization violation cannot be established under the required controls, so the finding is inconclusive.
